The '''floor function''', often denoted by $\lfloor \ \rfloor$, finds the largest integer no larger than a real number.

{{Hidden example}}
$$
\lfloor 4.5 \rfloor = 4 \\
\lfloor \pi \rfloor = 3 \\
\lfloor -1 \rfloor = -1 \\
$$
{{End hidden}}

== Formal definition ==

$$
\lfloor \ \rfloor: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{N},\\
\forall x \in \mathbb{R},\, \lfloor x \rfloor =
\begin{cases}
x, & x \in \mathbb{N},\\
\max(\{n\in \mathbb{N}| n<x\}), & \text{elsewise}.
\end{cases}
$$
